subject.title: Active Memory + Codex app-server path causes long response latency, hook timeouts, startup aborts, and gateway event-loop stalls

question: Should bundled Active Memory retain synchronous, parent-bound embedded recall before every eligible prompt, or should OpenClaw support a bounded fail-open recall path that is isolated from the parent Codex/native-hook runtime?
rationale: The report is a real reliability problem, but the remedy changes the plugin’s execution and recall semantics across Active Memory, embedded agents, provider routing, context engines, and native hooks; code review cannot choose that permanent product contract safely.

options.title: Adopt bounded fail-open recall
options.body: Make recall opportunistic or independently bounded so a missed recall never delays the parent reply or shares its runtime binding.

options.title: Retain blocking recall with hard isolation
options.body: Keep pre-prompt recall semantics but isolate its runtime/session resources and enforce prompt-cancellation behavior before the parent path is entered.

options.title: Keep current semantics and document mitigation
options.body: Preserve the existing architecture while documenting strict timeout and disablement guidance for Codex-backed deployments.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded fail-open recall
recommendation.body: Make recall opportunistic or independently bounded so a missed recall never delays the parent reply or shares its runtime binding.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the visible assigned routing point for the nearest open Active Memory reliability and embedded-run reports.
